plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous ornamental tree that covers its branches in clouds of delicate, fragrant blossoms before the leaves emerge. It is the most widely planted flowering cherry in Japan and a centerpiece of hanami celebrations.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in Japan; mid-March to April in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The famous cherry trees around the Tidal Basin in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and the National Cherry Blossom Festival is timed around their peak bloom.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers and gray-green strap-like leaves. It naturalizes readily in meadows, woodlands, and gardens, and is a classic herald of spring.
plants.location: Western Europe (England, Wales, France), naturalized across North America and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain lycorine and other alkaloids, making it toxic to most animals, which is why deer and rodents typically leave it alone.

plants.name: Magnolia × soulangeana
plants.description: A small deciduous tree or large shrub that produces large, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches in early spring. It is a hybrid of Magnolia denudata and Magnolia liliiflora, first raised in France in the 1820s.
plants.location: Cultivated across temperate regions of Europe, North America, and Asia
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, with fossil records dating back around 100 million years, predating bees, so they evolved to be pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into spectacular clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often carpeting streets and lawns with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere is Sept to Nov, but some populations in the northern tropics and in parts of South America bloom in March; in Australia and southern Africa, scattered late blooms occur
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Australia, South Africa, Mexico, and California
plants.funFact: In Mexico City, jacaranda trees famously bloom in March and April, painting the city purple, even though the species was introduced there in the early 1900s by a Japanese gardener.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the genus Protea, featuring a bowl of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny true flowers. It is adapted to fynbos fire-prone habitats.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly late summer to early winter in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering through March in many areas
plants.location: Southwestern and southern coastal regions of South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its thick underground lignotuber allows it to resprout after wildfires.
